text: Authorize gated phase-two diligence only. No token purchase yet. The core gates are the legal-entity map, securities classification, founders' vesting, market liquidity, traction verification, and control-function disclosure.

Gonka is a Bitcoin-style Proof of Work bet on decentralizing AI inference. The Liberman siblings, fresh from a Snap acquisition, built a Cosmos chain so that almost all compute goes to productive inference rather than consensus work. The thesis is that token incentives can break the centralized hyperscaler grip on inference.

Mainnet shipped in September 2025. CertiK audited three modules with no Critical findings. The project reports about eleven thousand H100-equivalent compute and one hundred million daily inference tokens. Bitfury validated the model with a fifty million dollar commitment. Independent third-party verification of throughput, node count, and developer count is still missing.

Differentiation is real, but the category is crowded with funded competitors. The Proof of Work alignment claim is design-philosophical. Host economics depend on token-price recovery. This is a market-formation bet, not a cash-flow asset.

The first gating issue is legal. The whitepaper is signed by a single individual with a personal email and names no entity. Five GNK distribution mechanisms each need their own legal theory. Only one is cleanly inside the SEC Proof of Work safe harbor.

The second gating issue is concentration. Twenty percent of supply sits in a founders' allocation with no public vesting. The token shows zero twenty-four-hour volume. The January high has fallen ninety percent.

The third gating issue is disclosure. Every traction figure is self-attributed. No general counsel, compliance officer, or head of security is publicly named. One CertiK centralization finding remains unresolved.

Proceed only when the structural gaps are closed. Real engineering and backing exist. Advance only if management delivers the entity map, counsel opinions, vesting schedule, named references, and control-function hires. Otherwise, pass.
